question.text: A stream of water has a width of 20 m and flows at 3 m/s. A small boat moves with a speed of 2√2 m/s relative to the water, directed at an angle of 45° with respect to the downstream flow.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Calculate the time needed for the boat to reach the opposite side.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the distance from the point straight across from the initial position to where the boat arrives on the opposite bank.

conditions: boat speed relative to water = 2√2 m/s
direction of boat relative to river current = 45°

solution.approach: Resolve the boat's velocity relative to water across and along the river; the across part fixes the crossing time, and the along part adds to the current to fix drift.

steps.text: Resolve the boat's velocity relative to water, 2√2 m/s at 45° to the current, into components across and along the river.
steps.equation: v_across = 2√2 sin45° = 2 m/s, v_along = 2√2 cos45° = 2 m/s

steps.text: The crossing time depends only on the across component, since that is what closes the 20 m width.
The ground velocity along the river is the current plus the boat's own along-river component, since both point the same way.
The drift is this along-river ground velocity times the crossing time; state both results.

common_mistakes.text: Using only the current speed for the drift and ignoring the boat's own along-river component gives 30 m instead of 50 m.
Using the full boat speed 2√2 m/s instead of only its across-river component to find the crossing time gives 7.1 s instead of 10 s.
